images.title: Same area, three shapes
images.purpose: Show three rectangles of 16 unit squares, 4 by 4, 8 by 2 and 16 by 1, with their borders outlined, so that the longer, thinner shapes visibly have the longer border.
images.composition: Three rectangles stacked, each with its border outlined and its area and perimeter written on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading Same area, three shapes in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Three rectangles stand one above the other, all made of 16 unit squares, with the unit square 36 by 36 px: (1) a rectangle of 4 by 4 unit squares, 144 by 144 px, at x 100 to 244 and y 120 to 264, filled teal #0072B2 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick amber #E69F00 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 4 by 4, Area 16 square units and Perimeter 16 units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937); (2) a rectangle of 8 by 2 unit squares, 288 by 72 px, at x 100 to 388 and y 340 to 412, filled teal #0072B2 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick amber #E69F00 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 8 by 2, Area 16 square units and Perimeter 20 units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937); (3) a rectangle of 16 by 1 unit squares, 576 by 36 px, at x 100 to 676 and y 490 to 526, filled teal #0072B2 with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines (2 px) and a thick amber #E69F00 outline (6 px) round its whole border; to its right, at x 760, the three lines of text 16 by 1, Area 16 square units and Perimeter 34 units, centred vertically on the rectangle (36 px, dark #1F2937). In all 3 rectangles and 48 unit squares counted over the three, 16 in each. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a rectangle with a number of unit squares other than 16, or rectangles drawn with different unit squares
a perimeter or area value other than the ones listed
images.takeaway: Shapes with the same area can have different perimeters: 16, 20 and 34 units for 16 squares.
images.description: Three rectangles of 16 unit squares, 4 by 4, 8 by 2 and 16 by 1, with perimeters 16, 20 and 34 units.
images.context: Concept image for Same Area, Different Perimeter. It follows the idea of the shapes of Let Us Explore in your maths book and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student trace each border with a finger and count its edges. The slip to watch: believing that equal areas must have equal borders.

image_decisions.why: The three outlined rectangles put 'same area, different border' in one look.
